summary: The macOS Debug 1.0.15+20 client initially remained on the guild startup screen. A read-only process sample and Unified Logging confirmed flutter_secure_storage was waiting for macOS Keychain authorization while reading session service v3. After the user manually unlocked the Mac, the same running client advanced into the authenticated SHARE_TEST room. The current ad-hoc app signature is not among the code hashes listed in the access-control prompt, consistent with authorization recurring after a rebuild. No Keychain items were changed and no password was collected.

checks.name: Current macOS Debug startup state
checks.observation: The running app (1.0.15+20, launched at 00:20 local time) still displayed 'Подключаемся к гильдии…' more than 12 minutes after launch.

checks.name: Read-only process sample of startup wait
checks.observation: The serial flutter_secure_storage_service queue was blocked in FlutterSecureStorage.read → SecItemCopyMatching → ItemImpl.getContent → CSSM_DecryptDataFinal → SecurityServer mach_msg. No cookie or secret values were inspected.

checks.name: Keychain authorization prompt confirmation
checks.command: /usr/bin/log show --last 20m --style compact --predicate '(process == securityd) AND eventMessage CONTAINS BOOHTACORD'
checks.observation: securityd logged 'displaying keychain prompt' for the app and service ru.boohtacord.boohtacordDesktop.session.v3. The logged ACL lists code-signature hashes that do not include the current Debug bundle CDHash; the bundle is ad-hoc signed with no TeamIdentifier. This supports the conclusion that a new build is requesting Keychain authorization.

checks.name: Keychain item safety
checks.observation: The diagnosis observed only the blocked read call stack and authorization metadata; no cookie value was returned or inspected. No Keychain item was deleted or modified, and no password was entered or collected.

checks.name: Public maintenance request avoids session Keychain access
checks.observation: A regression first failed because GET /maintenance read and sent the stored session cookie. It now uses only the public Origin/Accept headers. This removes an unnecessary Keychain read from startup and repeated five-second refreshes; the authenticated /auth/session check still needs the protected cookie and remains subject to the system prompt.

checks.name: Stalled startup session check leaves splash with actionable retry
checks.command: cd desktop && flutter test --no-pub test/app_state_test.dart --plain-name 'a stalled session check exits loading and offers a retryable error'
checks.observation: A test-injected 20 ms session timeout transitions AppState from loading to connectionError, exposes the retryable error and button, and advises macOS users to check Keychain authorization. The production timeout is 20 seconds. The timeout does not cancel the underlying native secure-storage call and does not restore access until Keychain authorization is resolved.

checks.name: Full Flutter suite and analyzer after startup timeout
checks.command: cd desktop && flutter test --no-pub && flutter analyze --no-pub
checks.observation: All 315 Flutter tests passed and analyzer reported no issues.

checks.name: Prompt-free startup without manual unlock or stable signature (initial blocked observation)
checks.observation: The app is waiting for the user to resolve the native Keychain access prompt, or for a Developer ID-signed build with a stable signing requirement. This host has no valid Developer ID signing identity.

checks.name: Current session after manual Mac unlock
checks.observation: After the user manually unlocked the Mac on 2026-10-01, the already-running BOOHTACORD client advanced from the guild-loading screen into the authenticated SHARE_TEST room and connected. Both voice participants were muted. Codex did not enter or collect a password. This does not prove prompt-free cold startup or persistence across a fresh app launch.

remaining: Repeat the startup check after a fresh app launch to establish normal latency and whether the Keychain authorization recurs; no stable Developer ID identity is available on this host. The public maintenance request no longer touches the session cookie, but cannot replace the protected session check.
